methods.limits: FFmpeg has to be configured with libtheora and libvorbis support.
The manual explains the container must change because theo and vorb are not compatible with MP4; it names the output sample_new.ogg, and .ogv is the recommended video extension.
Converts any media file ffmpeg can decode; without -o the output is named after the input with .ogv.

facts.fact: MP4 file format version 2 is ISO/IEC 14496-14:2003.
Ogg video uses video/ogg and the .ogv extension.
Ogg is a multimedia container maintained by Xiph.Org.
MP4 is built on the ISO Base Media File Format, grew out of QuickTime, commonly holds H.264 with AAC and can carry AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus; every major browser plays it.
MP4's registered media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4.
Xiph recommends .ogv for Ogg video.
Android plays HEVC video in MP4 files from version 5.0.

methods.steps: File > Export As (Shift+Ctrl+E), then export the image as AVIF.
methods.limits: GIMP added AVIF import and export in release 2.10.22; older releases lack it.
The formats page lists AVIF as read and write; magick identify -list format shows which formats a copy supports.
Accepts PNG input; -q sets quality on the tool's own scale; --lossless sets lossless defaults and emits warnings when settings or input do not allow it.

facts.fact: PNG became a W3C Recommendation in October 1996, was issued as RFC 2083 and ISO/IEC 15948, uses lossless DEFLATE, and supports 1 to 16 bits per sample with optional alpha.
The third edition of PNG became a W3C Recommendation on 24 June 2025, adds cICP for HDR and allows Exif in an eXIf chunk; software that cannot animate shows the default image of an APNG.
PNG's registered media types are image/png and image/apng.
macOS saves screenshots as PNG files by default.
AVIF stores AV1 images within HEIF and can include image sequences.
Chrome 85 added AVIF decoding.
Firefox 93 added AVIF image support.
Safari on iOS 16 added still AVIF images.
Android 12 and later support baseline 8-bit AVIF decoding.
Older browsers may fail to display AVIF; supply a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback.
PNG carries no known royalty-bearing patents and every major browser displays it.

methods.steps: Insert > Pictures > This Device, select the picture, then File > Save a Copy and update the name and file type.
methods.limits: The help page covers pictures in general and shows Save a Copy with an editable file type.

methods.steps: Choose Insert > Image, leave Link unchecked, insert the picture, then File > Save As and pick Word 2010-365 Document (.docx) as the file type.
methods.limits: A linked bitmap is reloaded whenever the document loads; saving to an external file type can lose some formatting.

facts.fact: DOCX is a ZIP-based Open XML package with document and media parts.
PNG pixel data differs from document text and layout; PNG was a W3C Recommendation from October 1996 and is ISO/IEC 15948.
PNG uses lossless DEFLATE, stores 1 to 16 bits per sample with optional alpha, starts with a fixed signature and is built from chunks.
macOS saves screenshots as PNG files by default.
Layer offsets may differ between GIMP and other applications; PNG compression setting does not reduce fidelity; camera tags and profiles are optional in GIMP exports.
PNG carries no known royalty-bearing patents and every major browser displays it.
The third edition of PNG became a W3C Recommendation on 24 June 2025 and allows Exif in an eXIf chunk.

methods.steps: Select a slide, File > Save As (Save a Copy on OneDrive or SharePoint), choose JPEG in the Save as Type list, Save, then Just This One or All Slides.
methods.limits: Each slide is saved as a separate file when you choose All Slides.

methods.steps: Open the slide in Normal view, File > Export, choose JPEG, Save Current Slide Only, optionally set width and height, Export.
methods.limits: Exports the current slide only.

methods.steps: File > Export To > Images, choose the slides, select an image format, Save, choose a location, Export.
methods.limits: Keynote opens .pptx and .ppt files; the help page does not list the image formats.

facts.fact: PPTX is PowerPoint's ordinary presentation type; macro-enabled presentations use .pptm; saving as an image flattens slide objects; saving as an older format can affect features.
PresentationML stores presentation content in an Office Open XML package; slides and relationships occupy separate parts; notes and slide masters have their own parts.
The media type is application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation.
JPEG does not retain layers or alpha.
Missing fonts can change the way a presentation displays; PowerPoint supports embedding eligible fonts.

methods.steps: File > Open the PSD, then File > Export As > JPG.
methods.limits: The Save for Web window lets you choose the output format and the resolution.

methods.steps: Drag the PSD into the Input tab, choose the target format and a destination folder on the Output tab, then click Convert.
methods.limits: The page names PSD as a format XnConvert can read; the progress report lists any files that failed.
[0] selects the first image of a file that holds several; quote the name because the brackets are special shell characters.

facts.fact: PSD is Adobe Photoshop's native format; signature 8BPS; image resources and layer information in separate sections; pixel data raw, RLE or ZIP; sample depths of 1, 8, 16 or 32 bits; 30,000 pixels per side, PSB raises it.
The registered PSD media type is image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.
JPEG is lossy and cannot retain alpha or multiple layers.

methods.steps: Open the XCF; choose Export from the File menu to write a JPEG; a dialog lets you set the quality.
methods.limits: Exporting does not save changes to the XCF; save the project separately.
-flatten composites the images onto a canvas in the background color; inspect the rendering against GIMP.

facts.fact: GIMP uses Save for XCF and Export for distribution formats.
XCF does not preserve undo history and is not an interchange format.
JPEG export is lossy and cannot store a layer stack.

methods.limits: Needs a decodable audio stream; -vn excludes video.

facts.fact: 3GP can hold sound, video and timed text.
3GPP permits AMR and AAC streams and uses ISO base media structure.
MP3 uses lossy audio coding.

methods.limits: AIFF-C reading still depends on the compression type inside the file.

facts.fact: AIFF-C extended the AIFF family for compressed audio in August 1991.
AIFC may also contain uncompressed samples and marker information.

methods.limits: Transcodes the selected video and sound; inspect multiple streams instead of assuming all are preserved.

facts.fact: ASF is Microsoft's wrapper for several kinds of audio and video streams.
The codec, rather than the container extension, determines media decoding requirements.

methods.limits: An index in square brackets selects an image from a multi-image file, counted from zero.
Pillow reads CUR and does not write it; animated cursors are not supported.

facts.fact: CUR uses per-image hotspots and may contain several image sizes.
PNG supports an alpha channel and lossless image coding.
